root_cause.reallocation_site: vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py:2465-2492 falls through to plan() for a non-cudagraph wrapper -> flashinfer/decode.py:3830-3837 rebinds _paged_kv_indptr_buf/_paged_kv_last_page_len_buf and reallocates _qo_indptr_buf on every plan
root_cause.why_the_draft: the V2 speculator drafts one token per request per step, so its decode graphs are captured at q_len==1 (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py:345 dispatches with uniform_token_count=1) while the scalar is 1+3=4
root_cause.also_latent: under num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size the target captures one verify shape per depth (8 sizes x 2 depths on this profile); every depth whose q_len != 1+num_spec_tokens had the same exposure
root_cause.fault_surface: the async fault is reported at the next sync point, vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py:312 seq_lens.to('cpu'); under CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 it lands in cudagraph_utils.py:589 graphs[desc].replay(). Messenger, not culprit - confirmed, unchanged from the filing
root_cause.predecessor_lead: confirmed and refined: the FlashInfer plan-buffer capture/replay identity hazard was the right family; the specific defect is the scalar q_len gate, not build_for_cudagraph_capture vs build routing

card_docs_text_handed_to_main.card_paragraph: **V2 model runner + MTP-3 depth schedule (measured, PR'd).** The V2 model runner would not start with MTP-3 on this checkpoint: the speculator's captured draft-decode CUDA graph replayed against freed FlashInfer plan buffers (cudaErrorIllegalAddress), because persistent decode wrappers were admitted only for q_len == 1 + num_speculative_tokens while draft steps run q_len == 1. Keying those wrappers by the shape capture actually planned fixes it (local-inference-lab/vllm#398, closes #396). With the fix, one server running the per-batch-size depth schedule (depth 3 at batch 1-2, depth 1 at batch 3-8) measures 87.4 tok/s at C1 and 416.3 tok/s at C8 on a single RTX 5090 - +38.0 % aggregate decode at C8 against an MRV1 baseline measured in the same window (301.6 tok/s), i.e. depth-1 throughput at batch 8 without giving up depth-3 latency at batch 1. Constraint: at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 the V2 runner has no headroom and the EXL3 prefill reconstruct OOMs on the first 2,048-token prefill (both arms, schedule off and on), so today the win needs a context/KV concession - measured at 131,072 max context and 0.95 utilisation, giving 234,256 KV tokens against 272,570 on the published profile (-14.1 %). Greedy outputs repeat identically within an engine process; cross-restart bit-exactness is not claimable on this stack (exl3_gemm autotune per process, same caveat as the scratch-arena note).
card_docs_text_handed_to_main.docs_41_W1_sentence: W1 is no longer closed-as-unavailable: the blocker was a fork-local FlashInfer gate that captured and replayed the V2 speculator's draft-decode graph on the dynamic decode wrapper (fixed in local-inference-lab/vllm#398, closes #396, root cause proven with an instrumented capture-vs-replay address log plus a pinned-buffer causality control). Both W1 arms now serve and complete the full probe; the depth schedule measures +38.0 % aggregate decode at C8 (416.29 vs 301.63 tok/s matched in-window baseline) with C1 held at 87.35 tok/s, confirming and exceeding the inherited +30.67 % estimate - but only at 131,072/0.95, because at the published 262,144/0.97 profile the V2 runner OOMs in the EXL3 prefill reconstruct on the first 2,048-token prefill.
card_docs_text_handed_to_main.one_sentence_if_only_one_fits: The V2 runner's MTP-3 crash was a FlashInfer persistent-decode-wrapper gate that admitted only q_len == 1 + num_speculative_tokens, so the draft-decode graph (q_len == 1) was captured and replayed on the dynamic wrapper whose plan buffers move; keying wrappers by the captured shape (local-inference-lab/vllm#398) unblocks the per-batch-size depth schedule, measured at 87.4 tok/s C1 and 416.3 tok/s C8 in one server (+38.0 % at C8), at the cost of 14.1 % KV tokens because 0.97 utilisation OOMs the EXL3 prefill reconstruct under V2.
